Close (both sides): 28:19 ends "כָּל יוֹדְעֶ֨יךָ֙ בָּֽעַמִּ֔ים שָׁמְמ֖וּ עָלֶ֑יךָ בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔יתָ וְאֵינְךָ֖ עַד עוֹלָֽם" (oshb:Ezek.28.19) with a PE immediately after and no recognition/utterance/"I YHWH have spoken" formula present; the close pattern “You have become a terror, and you will exist no more.” (web:Ezek.28.19, WEB) mirrors MT 27:36's terminal clause in the CONSONANTAL Hebrew and not in the translation - MEASURED from Ezek_oshb.txt, the two verses end consonant for consonant on the same four words and differ only in the Masoretic pointing, feminine singular at MT 27:36 against masculine singular at MT 28:19, while the WEB renders MT 27:36 quite differently as “You have come to a terrible end, and you will be no more.” (web:Ezek.27.36, WEB); the earlier claim of an exact mirror held only of the Hebrew and is scoped here. Behind, 28:10 closed the prince-of-Tyre unit on the stacked "I have spoken" + utterance close and a SAMEKH; ahead, 28:20 opens a fresh strict word-event onset for the Sidon oracle.
why: Two A6 installs, and one claim narrowed to what the bytes support. MEASURED: each run is the WEB rendering at exactly one verse book-wide (28:12 and 28:19), both in this row's span. The row's mirrors-27:36-exactly claim was true of the consonantal Hebrew and false of the WEB, which renders the two verses with different English; the sentence now says which witness the mirror holds in and discloses the pointing difference. web:Ezek.27.36 is a far-side reference under DEF-A4-ARGUED clause 4, outside the window [28:10, 28:20]: recorded, never a defect.
tier: MEASURED (tools/verse_map_web.json) for both runs; MEASURED (Ezek_oshb.txt) for the consonantal identity and the pointing difference
